contributions.statement: After each agent write, drop held copies of the symbols that write changed; in Claude Code trajectories most held context was unneeded and mostly stale, while over half of the needed context was missing.
contributions.evidence: Table 5/§3.1.2: 73.4% of held tokens unneeded, 72.3% of those stale, 58.5% of gold tokens missing; silver labels (rules + gpt-5.4 oracle), human review queue not yet filled; one agent, 48 instances.

contributions.statement: Use a small model as a side-car context manager for the main agent.
contributions.evidence: Table 4: manager overhead 0.8-4.7% of main-agent tokens; end-to-end margins often one task or <1pt, single runs.

reason: Write-conditioned staleness is a plausible, new framing, but its evidence rests on silver labels the authors say are not yet human-reviewed, and end-to-end wins are within noise.
